description.narrative: 12.4% of Uganda’s population are persons with disabilities(approximately 4.5million). Since 1998 when the government ofUganda introduced affirmative action scheme to all publicuniversities, several of PWDs have had an opportunities to attainhigher education either at diploma or degree level. At everyacademic year, 64 students with disabilities get entry into thegovernment universities and some of these are Persons with BrainInjury (PWABIs). Despite this ever increasing number of PWDsattaining professional carriers in different fields, the government hasnot put in place measures to ensure that PWDs are recruited in theexisting labor market either for government or in the private sector.As other abled bodied have gained meaningful employment, severalPWDs have been left jobless aftera hard gain professional careerdue to several reasons such as negative attitudes of employers, in-accessible work places, lack of enough confidence among theemployable PWDs to compete for jobs, discriminatory interviewprocess, among others. Although PWBIs may noteasily berecognized as a particular disability, face more challenges ofaccessing formal employment due to their unique needs such aseasily get tired, not comfortable with too much noise which rendersthem more disadvantaged in the existing labor market. The mainproject objective: “to ensure increased access and retention toformal employment by Persons with Brian Injury” in the labor marketBISOU wishes change in the following dimensions:Improved/strengthened capacity ofBrain Injury SupportOrganization to promote inclusive employment for people withdisabilities, particularly PWBI, Increased number ofcandidates/primary beneficiaries (PWDs) who feel betterpreparedand more confident to access waged employment, Employers inthetargeted area (Kayunga District) have increased understandingondisability employment rights and infrastructure adaptations, At least12 PWBI have accessed formal employment in both governmentand private sector in Kayunga district.

participating-org.narrative:
BISU is a Community Based Organisation for persons with disabilities specifically persons with brain injury (PWBIs) which begun in 2018 and officially registered in 2011 with key operations in Kayunga District. The spirit of start of the organization wasignited by a parent in the area who had a child with brain injury, and through the several efforts of seeking rehabilitation of his child realized that there are other parents with children, adults of the same disability. This motivated the parent to mobilize such parents,but also adults of the above disabilities and begun the organisation as a strategy/voice of others for easy advocacy and lobbying for services for Persons with Brain Injury (PWBI). The organisation put in place elementary structures like Board, and small secretariat, and begun fundraising for resources to fulfil their mandate. Therefore, BISU was formed as a membership organisation for PWBI, representing one of the most invisible disabilities in Uganda. BISU is gender sensitive organisation in relation to the categories of people involved in the development of the community. Much effort and focus is on diversity during the recruitment process, create fair compensation and promotion procedures, Offering flexible and supportive employeeand victim benefits and building an inclusive organizational culture which favours individuals, clients and victims regardless of their gender. By doing this we promote relationships between the workspace and the families in the community thus involving them in all activities to promote awareness and give maximum aid to PWBIs.
PWBIs are quite invisible, very difficult to identify and assess their disabilities unless very close to them or their relatives. However, BISU has been able to identity so far 64PWBIs in Kayunga district, captured in the database and linking them to different referral centres for support. These members are referred to Baale Main Hospital, especially children for physco-social support and habilitation in the neurosurgery ward. While other are also linked, advocated or connected to schools for enrolment for education, currently 6 children secured bursaries in schools and are studying to chase for their academic career. This has very profiled BISU in the area as an organisation specialized in supporting PWBIs.
Secondly, registration of BISU with the NGO Bureau which means that organisation can fully operate and run her activities within her jurisdiction to support the membership. The physical address of BISU is situated in Kayunga district, Baale Sub-county, Gayaza Trading Centre.
Lastly, through the fundraising efforts, BISU was able to secure a grant from DRF to embark on the campaign of advocating for enrolment of PWBIs in primary schools of the districts and so far 6 learners from very impoverished families are in schools like any other child in the community. UNAPD also advanced a trust fund to the organisation for institutional strengthening which enabled in developing simple operational financial guidelines/account systems.
